    Dilatant Dark Fluid (DDF) Quantum-Hydrodynamic Model #

    This module formalizes the core mathematical framework of the Dilatant Dark Fluid (DDF) proposed by Marco Fedi (2026), Dilatant Dark Fluid: Toward a Unified Quantum-Hydrodynamic Origin of Lorentz Invariance, Gravity, and Cosmological Phenomenology (SSRN Preprint 7406660).

    The framework models spacetime and gravitation as emergent phenomena of a two-component quantum-hydrodynamic substrate:

    1. Continuous Superfluid Phase (ϕ): A coherent BEC supporting quantized vortices (matter particles) and circulatory Bernoulli pressure/enthalpy deficits (gravity).
    2. Dispersed Dilatant Phase (φ): A heavier dispersed phase exhibiting shear-thickening and shear-jamming. In the saturated state, it supports transverse phonons propagating at speed c (identified with photons).
    3. Constitutive Lorentz Factor: Moving bodies experience longitudinal sheath compression Λ_∥(v) = γ_φ(v) = 1/√(1 - v²/c²), yielding relativistic kinetic energy, clock dilation, and the operational Minkowski interval.
    4. Painlevé-Gullstrand River Geometry: Inflow superflow v_r = -√(2GM/r) encodes Schwarzschild exterior geometry with acoustic horizon at r_H = 2GM/c², and dipolar swirl encodes Kerr-Lense-Thirring dragging.
    5. Galactic Isothermal Regime: Superfluid isothermal barotrope yields flat rotation curves v_flat = √(q_ρ) * c_ϕ without dark matter halos.
    6. Decisive Discriminator: Radiation active gravitational sourcing parameter η_act^γ = 0 in DDF versus 1 in GR.

          Moving Sheath and Jamming-Based Lorentz Kinematics #

          source
          structure Signals.DDF.MovingSheath (sub : DDFSubstrate) :
          Type

          A massive configuration translating through the dispersed φ background at a subluminal relative speed.

          • velocity : ℝ
          • velocity_nonneg : 0 ≤ self.velocity
          • subluminal : self.velocity < sub.c
          Instances For
            source
            noncomputable def Signals.DDF.MovingSheath.betaSq {sub : DDFSubstrate} (s : MovingSheath sub) :
            ℝ

            The speed ratio squared β² = (v / c)².

            Instances For
              source
              theorem Signals.DDF.MovingSheath.one_sub_betaSq_pos {sub : DDFSubstrate} (s : MovingSheath sub) :
              0 < 1 - s.betaSq

              The factor 1 - v²/c² is strictly positive for subluminal motion.

              source
              noncomputable def Signals.DDF.MovingSheath.jammingFactor {sub : DDFSubstrate} (s : MovingSheath sub) :
              ℝ

              The speed-dependent constitutive jamming factor γ_φ(v) = 1 / √(1 - v²/c²).

              Instances For
                source
                theorem Signals.DDF.MovingSheath.jammingFactor_pos {sub : DDFSubstrate} (s : MovingSheath sub) :
                0 < s.jammingFactor

                The jamming factor is strictly positive.

                source

                                                                    Constructive Solutions to Critiques 1–3 & Unified $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2, 4)$–DDF Integration #

                                                                    This section resolves all three critique issues constructively and integrates the complex Grassmannian $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2, 4)$ directly with DDFSubstrate, MovingSheath, Madelung condensate densities, and RiverExterior frame-dragging:

                                                                    1. Resolution of Critique 1 (ddf_critique1_solved_squared_crossing_and_complex_gr24):
                                                                      • In real $Gr(2,4)$, interpreting the channel weights $Q_A, Q_B$ as coherent field amplitudes makes the on-axis intensity proportional to the squared crossing product $(\Delta_{02}\Delta_{13})^2 = (Q_A + Q_B)^2 = 4$, achieving exact zero relative error ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$) at the symmetric point $(0, 0)$.
                                                                      • Across the entire detector plane $(x, y) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, lifting to complex sink amplitudes $w_A^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{\mathbb{C}}) = \Delta_{01}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{23}^{\mathbb{C}}$ and $w_B^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{\mathbb{C}}) = \Delta_{03}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{12}^{\mathbb{C}}$ on $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ satisfies $w_A^{\mathbb{C}} + w_B^{\mathbb{C}} = \Delta_{02}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{13}^{\mathbb{C}}$, so $|\Delta_{02}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{13}^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = |w_A^{\mathbb{C}} + w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2$ achieves zero relative predictive error everywhere.
                                                                    2. Resolution of Critique 2 (ddf_critique2_solved_projective_and_trace_renormalized_jamming):
                                                                      • Projectively normalizing by the crossing product via gr24ProjectiveBarycentricShift ($\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{bary}} = (Q_A - Q_B)/(Q_A + Q_B)$) and gr24ProjectiveVisibilitySq cancels the $e^{2(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)t}$ dilation factor identically, making $\widehat{d}_{\mathrm{bary}}$ and $\widehat{\mathcal{V}}_{Gr(2,4)}^2$ exact invariants under arbitrary non-symplectic compressive jamming $\operatorname{diag}(e^{\lambda_1 t}, e^{\lambda_2 t})$.
                                                                      • Factoring out the isotropic trace dilation $e^{-(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2)t / 2}$ reduces any diagonal jamming matrix to the symplectic Anosov matrix $A_{\mathrm{Anosov}}((\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)/2, t)$, which preserves even the unnormalized Plücker minors.
                                                                    3. Resolution of Critique 3 (MovingSheath.ddf_critique3_solved_substrate_parameter_recovery & RiverExterior.quantized_vortex_swirl_from_circulation):
                                                                      • Connects the optical relative error $\varepsilon = (1 - \mathcal{V}(s))/2$ directly to the dimensionful DDF substrate parameters $\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi = c^{-2}$ and physical sheath speed $v$: $\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi v^2 = 4\varepsilon(1 - \varepsilon)$, $v^2 = 4\varepsilon(1 - \varepsilon) / (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)$, and $\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi = 4\varepsilon(1 - \varepsilon) / v^2$ (for $v \neq 0$).
                                                                      • Connects the differential OAM vortex circulation $\Delta\Gamma(\ell_1, \ell_2)$ to the Kerr/Lense--Thirring gravitomagnetic swirl velocity in RiverExterior: $v_{\phi,\mathrm{swirl}}((\ell_2 - \ell_1)\hbar, r) = \frac{G_\phi m_\phi \varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi}{\pi r^2}\,\Delta\Gamma(\ell_1, \ell_2)$.
                                                                    4. Unified $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2, 4)$–DDF Sheath Twistor Formalism (MovingSheath.gr24TwistorMatrix):
                                                                      • Embeds any subluminal MovingSheath $s$ and differential OAM vortex charge $\Delta\ell$ into $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$, proving that its Madelung channel densities are $|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 + v/c$ and $|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 - v/c$, their product is $\gamma_\varphi(v)^{-2}$, its crossing minor reproduces the DDF shear-jammed OAM intensity $I_{\mathrm{HS,OAM}}(x,y,\phi;\Delta\ell,\gamma_\varphi(v)^{-1})$ with zero relative error everywhere, and $SL(2, \mathbb{C})$ / complex Anosov transformations preserve the crossing-minor intensity identically.

                                                                                Planetary Orbits, Mercury Perihelion Precession, BCJ Double Copy, $N$-Body Dynamics, & $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$–DDF Bridge #

                                                                                Formalizes the orbital mechanics, post-Minkowskian QED/gauge double-copy scattering, and Dilatant Dark Fluid (DDF) connections for planetary orbits (docs/grassmannian-gravity-from-qed-scattering-paper.md):

                                                                                1. Keplerian & Post-Newtonian / QFT / DDF Orbital Geometry (PlanetaryOrbit):
                                                                                  • Semi-latus rectum $p = a(1 - e^2)$, perihelion $r_{\min} = a(1 - e)$, aphelion $r_{\max} = a(1 + e)$, harmonic-mean identity $2/p = 1/r_{\min} + 1/r_{\max}$, geometric-mean identity $r_{\min} r_{\max} = a p$, and Kepler's third law $T^2 / a^3 = 4\pi^2 / (G_\phi M)$.
                                                                                2. Effective Relativistic / QFT / DDF Potential & Anomalous Perihelion Precession:
                                                                                  • The effective central potential $V_{\mathrm{eff}}(r) = -\frac{G_\phi M m}{r}\bigl(1 + \frac{3 L^2}{m^2 c^2 r^2}\bigr)$ decomposes into the superfluid Bernoulli enthalpy $m \Phi_\phi(r)$ plus the 1-loop / DDF shear-jamming $r^{-3}$ correction $-\frac{3 G_\phi M L^2 \varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi}{m r^3}$.
                                                                                  • Anomalous perihelion precession per orbit: $$\Delta\varpi = \frac{6\pi G_\phi M}{c^2 a(1 - e^2)} = \frac{3\pi\,r_H}{a(1 - e^2)} = \frac{6\pi\,G_\phi M\,\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi}{a(1 - e^2)},$$ together with the solar-system planetary scaling law $\frac{\Delta\varpi(p_1)}{\Delta\varpi(p_2)} = \frac{p_2}{p_1}$ and Mercury's validated $\approx 42.98''/\text{century}$ benchmark.
                                                                                3. BCJ Color–Kinematics Duality & Plücker $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Double-Copy Bridge:
                                                                                  • In 4-point gauge/gravity scattering, the BCJ kinematic Jacobi relation $n_s - n_t + n_u = 0$ is realized directly by the 3-term complex Plücker identity $\Delta_{01}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{23}^{\mathbb{C}} - \Delta_{02}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{13}^{\mathbb{C}} + \Delta_{03}^{\mathbb{C}}\Delta_{12}^{\mathbb{C}} = 0$ on $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$, and squaring the Plücker channel numerators generates the symmetric graviton/fluid-tension double-copy amplitude.
                                                                                4. Complex $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Orbital Precession Twistor Matrix (PlanetaryOrbit.gr24PrecessionMatrix):
                                                                                  • Encoding orbital eccentricity $e \in [0, 1)$ as the $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ barycentric shift ($d_{\mathrm{bary}} = e$) and the anomalous perihelion phase $\Delta\varpi / 2$ in $M_{\mathbb{C}}(z_{\mathrm{aph}}, z_{\mathrm{per}}) \in Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ makes the Madelung channel densities equal the normalized aphelion and perihelion radii $|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 + e = r_{\max}/a$ and $|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 - e = r_{\min}/a$, while their product $|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 |w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2 = 1 - e^2 = p / a$ is the exact semi-latus rectum ratio governing $\Delta\varpi = 3\pi r_H / p$.
                                                                                5. $N$-Body Gravitational Sink-Flow Superposition & Conservative vs. Dissipative Critique:
                                                                                  • Formalizes $N$-body Bernoulli sink superposition $\Phi_\phi^{(N)} = -\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} \frac{G_\phi M_i}{r_i}$, total secular perihelion advance $\Delta\varpi_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Delta\varpi_{\mathrm{rel}} + \sum_{j} \Delta\varpi_{j,\mathrm{Newtonian}}$ (matching Mercury's $42.98'' + 531.63'' = 574.61''/\text{century}$), and proves that conservative DDF action preserves orbital energy ($\Delta E = 0$) whereas non-conservative Stokes drag causes secular orbital energy decay ($dE/dt = -F_d v < 0$). (The DDF-independent QED/gauge BCJ double copy, PlanetaryOrbit geometry, gr24PrecessionMatrix, and flat-space gravitational-wave theorems live in Signals.QEDGravity and are re-exported in Signals.DDF.)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Unified $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(3, 6)$ Simultaneous Splitting Conservation, Holographic Perspective Projection, and Inversion-Free Schur–Plücker Theorem: Extends the full suite of simultaneous conservation, holographic projection, and Schur–Plücker laws from $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2, 4)$ to higher-rank $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(3, 6)$:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1. $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(3, 6)$ Adaptive 3D Splat-Splitting Conservation Laws (M3_plus = c_plus.gr36TwistorMatrix φ1 φ2 φ3):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC1: $|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = |\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,-})|^2 = \frac{1}{4}|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC2: $(x_+ - x_c)^2 + (y_+ - y_c)^2 + (z_+ - z_c)^2 + |\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = |\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 = \sigma_1^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC3: $|\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$, $|\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = |\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$, and $|\Delta_{312}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = |\Delta_{312}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC4: $|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = \frac{1}{4}|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$ and $|\Delta_{042}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = \frac{1}{4}|\Delta_{042}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC5: $|\Delta_{012}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,+})|^2 = \frac{1}{4}|\Delta_{012}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 = c_+.\mathrm{covDet}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SC6: $c_+.\operatorname{coreBohmPotential}(m, \hbar) - \mathrm{splat}.\operatorname{coreBohmPotential}(m, \hbar) = \frac{3\hbar^2}{4m\,|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2. $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(3, 6)$ Holographic Perspective Projection & Tomographic Depth Recovery (M3_persp = splat.gr36PerspectiveTwistorMatrix f φ1 φ2 φ3):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-HP1: $|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 = s_{\mathrm{persp}}.\mathrm{covDet} = (f/z_c)^4 |\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-HP2: $|\Delta_{012}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 = |\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 \, |\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 = (f/z_c)^4 |\Delta_{012}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-HP3: $\frac{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 - |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2}{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 + |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2} = \frac{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 - |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2}{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 + |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-HP4: $\frac{|\Delta_{012}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2}{|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2} = |\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 = \sigma_3^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-HP5: $f^2 \, \frac{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2 + |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3)|^2}{|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2 + |\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_3^{\mathrm{persp}})|^2} = z_c^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3. $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(3, 6)$ Inversion-Free Schur–Plücker Determinant Calculus (M3_schur = gr36SchurShearMatrix τ φ1 φ2 φ3):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SP1: $|\Delta_{045}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2 = 1 + \tau$ and $|\Delta_{315}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2 = 1 - \tau$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SP2: $|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2 = 1 - \tau^2 = \det(\operatorname{impellerShear4x4}(s, \tau))$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SP3: $|\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2 = \operatorname{schurComplement3DVolume}(\tau) = \frac{\bigl(|\Delta_{015}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2\bigr)^2}{1 + \tau^2}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • G3-SP4: $\det\Sigma_{4\times 4} = (\Sigma_{4\times 4})_{3,3} \cdot |\Delta_{342}^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{3,\tau})|^2$,

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Superfluid Gross–Pitaevskii Action, Madelung Polar Substitution, Variational Continuity & Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi Equations, and Dilatant-Phase ($\varphi$) Jamming Recovery #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    This section bridges the variable-level Madelung decomposition (madelungDensity, madelungAmplitude, madelungPhase, bohmQuantumPotential, superfluidVelocity) to an explicit variational action principle and dilatant-phase ($\varphi$) coupling:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1. Superfluid Gross–Pitaevskii / NLS Action & Madelung Polar Substitution ($\psi = A e^{i\theta} = \sqrt{\rho} e^{i S / \hbar}$): Substituting the polar order parameter $\psi = A(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$ and its chain-rule derivative $\partial_\mu\psi = (\partial_\mu A + i A\,\partial_\mu\theta)e^{i\theta}$ into the complex Gross–Pitaevskii Lagrangian density $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GP}} = \frac{i\hbar}{2}\bigl(\psi^*\partial_t\psi - \psi\partial_t\psi^*\bigr) - \frac{\hbar^2}{2 m_\phi}|\nabla\psi|^2 - V_{\mathrm{ext}}|\psi|^2 - \frac{g_\phi}{2}|\psi|^4$$ identically transforms the temporal symplectic term into $-\hbar A^2 \dot{\theta} = -\rho\,\partial_t S$ and splits the spatial gradient norm squared into $|\nabla A|^2 + A^2|\nabla\theta|^2$, yielding the real hydrodynamic Lagrangian density $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}(\rho, \nabla\rho, \partial_t S, \nabla S)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2. Euler–Lagrange Variations Yield Continuity & Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi (QHJ) Equations:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Varying $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}$ with respect to the action phase $S$ (where $\pi_S = \partial\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}} / \partial(\partial_t S) = -\rho$ and $J_S = \partial\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}} / \partial(\nabla S) = -\rho v_\phi$) yields the exact compressible continuity equation $\partial_t\rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho v_\phi) = 0$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • Varying $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}$ with respect to the real amplitude $A = \sqrt{\rho}$ (or density $\rho = A^2$ via the Fisher-information identity) yields the exact Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi (QHJ) equation $$\partial_t S + \frac{1}{2}m_\phi v_\phi^2 + V_{\mathrm{ext}} + g_\phi\rho + Q(\rho) = 0, \qquad Q(\rho) = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2 m_\phi}\frac{\Delta\sqrt{\rho}}{\sqrt{\rho}},$$ whose stationary coarse-grained limit ($\partial_t S = 0, g_\phi = 0, \Delta\sqrt{\rho} = 0$) recovers the Painlevé–Gullstrand Bernoulli potential $\Phi_\phi(r) = -\frac{1}{2}v_\phi(r)^2 = -\frac{G_\phi M}{r}$ of RiverExterior.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3. Dilatant-Phase ($\varphi$) Coupling & Variational Recovery of DDF Jamming $\Lambda_\parallel(v) = \gamma_\varphi(v)$: Coupling a translating vortex sheath ($v < c$) to the dispersed dilatant $\varphi$-substrate defines the sheath-compression Euler–Lagrange residual $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{sheath}}(\Lambda_\parallel) = \Lambda_\parallel(1 - \beta^2) - \Lambda_\parallel^{-1}$ and convex variational excess $\Delta\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sheath}}(\Lambda_\parallel) = \frac{1}{2}m c^2(1 - \beta^2)(\Lambda_\parallel - \gamma_\varphi(v))^2 \ge 0$, whose unique stationary minimum at $\Lambda_\parallel > 0$ is $\Lambda_\parallel = \gamma_\varphi(v) = (1 - v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. Evaluating the worldline dilatant Lagrangian $L_{\mathrm{DDF}}(v) = -m c^2 / \gamma_\varphi(v)$ derives the clock proper-time law $d\tau_D = (-L_{\mathrm{DDF}}(v)/(m c^2))dt = dt / \gamma_\varphi(v)$ (discharging the h_dtau assumption of material_minkowski_interval), recovers $H_{\mathrm{DDF}}(v) = \gamma_\varphi(v)m c^2 = m c^2 + K_D(v)$ via Legendre transformation, and links $\bigl(L_{\mathrm{DDF}}(v)/(-m c^2)\bigr)^2 = 1 - v^2/c^2$ directly to the $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ uncrossed Plücker product $|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Madelung Variational Action, Continuity & Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi Euler–Lagrange Equations, and Dilatant-Phase ($\varphi$) Jamming Recovery Theorem: Establishes the complete dynamics-level bridge from the superfluid Gross–Pitaevskii action and Madelung polar substitution $\psi = A e^{i S / \hbar}$ to the continuity equation, Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi (QHJ) equation, dilatant sheath jamming law $\Lambda_\parallel = \gamma_\varphi(v)$, action-derived Minkowski interval, and complex Grassmannian $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Plücker invariants:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. Exact Polar Substitution in the Gross–Pitaevskii Lagrangian Density: For $\psi = \operatorname{madelungPolarWavefunction}(A, S/\hbar)$, $\partial_t\psi = \operatorname{madelungPolarDerivative}(A, \dot{A}, S/\hbar, \partial_t S / \hbar)$, and $\nabla\psi = \operatorname{madelungPolarDerivative}(A, \nabla A, S/\hbar, \nabla S / \hbar)$ ($\hbar \neq 0$):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $|\psi|^2 = A^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $-\hbar\,\operatorname{Im}(\psi^*\partial_t\psi) = -A^2\,\partial_t S$ (independent of $\dot{A}$),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $|\nabla\psi|^2 = (\nabla A)^2 + A^2(\nabla S / \hbar)^2$, and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GP}}(\psi, \partial_t\psi, \nabla\psi) = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}(A, \nabla A, \partial_t S, \nabla S) = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}^\rho(A^2, 2 A\nabla A, \partial_t S, \nabla S)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2. Euler–Lagrange Phase & Amplitude Variations Yield Continuity & QHJ Equations:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Varying $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}$ with respect to $S$ yields $\operatorname{madelungPhaseEulerLagrangeResidual}(-\partial_t\rho, -\nabla\cdot(\rho v_\phi)) = \operatorname{madelungContinuityResidual}(\partial_t\rho, \nabla\cdot(\rho v_\phi))$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • Varying $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Mad}}$ with respect to $A > 0$ yields $\frac{\operatorname{madelungAmplitudeEulerLagrangeResidual}(m_\phi, \hbar, g_\phi, V_{\mathrm{ext}}, A, \Delta A, \partial_t S, \nabla S)}{-2 A} = \operatorname{quantumHamiltonJacobiResidual}(m_\phi, \hbar, g_\phi, V_{\mathrm{ext}}, A, \Delta A, \partial_t S, \nabla S / m_\phi)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the stationary coarse-grained RiverExterior limit ($\partial_t S = 0, g_\phi = 0, \Delta A = 0$), $\operatorname{quantumHamiltonJacobiResidual}(m_\phi, \hbar, 0, m_\phi\cdot re.\mathrm{bernoulliPotential}(r), A, 0, 0, re.\mathrm{velocity}(r)) = 0$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3. Dilatant-Phase ($\varphi$) Coupling Uniquely Recovers DDF Jamming $\Lambda_\parallel = \gamma_\varphi(v)$:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • At $\Lambda_\parallel = s.\mathrm{jammingFactor}$, $s.\mathrm{sheathCompressionResidual}(\gamma_\varphi(v)) = 0$ and $s.\mathrm{sheathVariationalExcess}(m, \gamma_\varphi(v)) = 0$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • For any $\Lambda_\parallel > 0$, $s.\mathrm{sheathCompressionResidual}(\Lambda_\parallel) = 0 \iff \Lambda_\parallel = s.\mathrm{jammingFactor}$, and $0 \le s.\mathrm{sheathVariationalExcess}(m, \Lambda_\parallel)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                4. Legendre Hamiltonian, Mass-Shell Invariant, Action-Derived Proper Time, & $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Plücker Duality:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $s.\mathrm{dilatantHamiltonian}(m) = \gamma_\varphi(v) m c^2 = m c^2 + s.\mathrm{kineticEnergy}(m)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • $(s.\mathrm{dilatantHamiltonian}(m))^2 - c^2(s.\mathrm{dilatantCanonicalMomentum}(m))^2 = (m c^2)^2$,

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Madelung Field Legendre Hamiltonian, QHJ-to-Euler Momentum Bridge, $\text{AdS}_5$/DDF Plücker Lapse, and $405\text{ nm}/532\text{ nm}$ STED Nanolithography Quantum-Confinement Theorem: Resolves and connects four cross-domain structural bridges:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{Mad}}^\rho(A^2, 2A\nabla A, \nabla S / m_\phi) = \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{Mad}}(A, \nabla A, \nabla S)$, and

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         Gravitational Waves With DDF: Dispersed-Phase ($\varphi$) Strain & Luminosity Decomposition, GPE Vortex Secondary Scattering, Kelvin-Wave Tail Damping, TT vs. Jammed Tensor Splats, and 4D Schur-Complement Conditioning #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Formalizes the quantum-hydrodynamic extensions of quadrupole gravitational-wave generation and propagation inside a DDFSubstrate (data/chats/Review-Pop-III-GW-Remnants.md, lines 389–855; data/chats/SQGDDF-Explanation-of-Wave-Delays.md, lines 1–115), contrasted directly against the flat-space QED/gauge double-copy model in Signals.QEDGravity:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        1. DDF Acoustic-Horizon & Dispersed-Phase ($\varphi$) Strain and Luminosity Decomposition: Using $c^2 = (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)^{-1}$ (DDFSubstrate.c_sq), the quadrupole strain amplitude $h_0$ and 2.5PN Peters–Mathews luminosity $P_{\mathrm{GW}}$ decompose into powers of the dispersed-phase jamming density $\varrho_{\max}^\varphi$ and minimum compressibility $j_{\min}^\varphi$: $$h_0^{\mathrm{DDF}} = \frac{r_{H,1}\,r_{H,2}}{R\,a} = \frac{4 G_\phi^2 M m_2 (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)^2}{R\,a}, \qquad (P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{DDF}})^2 = \left(\frac{32}{5}\frac{G_\phi^4 M^2 m_2^2(M+m_2)}{a^5}\right)^2 (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)^5\,\frac{P_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2}{\bigl(|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}|^2|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}|^2\bigr)^7}.$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        2. Breakdown of Huygens' Principle via GPE Vortex Density-Gradient Scattering: Around a quantized GPE vortex of healing length $\xi = \hbar / \sqrt{2 m_\phi g_0 \rho_0}$, the radial condensate density $\rho_{\mathrm{vortex}}(r) = \rho_0 \frac{r^2}{r^2 + \xi^2}$ vanishes at the core ($r = 0$), reaches $\rho_0 / 2$ at $r = \xi$, and creates a strictly positive acoustic refractive-index gradient $V_{\mathrm{scat}}(r) = \frac{2\rho_0\xi^2 r}{(r^2+\xi^2)^2} > 0$ for all $r > 0$, continuously generating secondary Huygens wavelets (gravitational tails).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        3. Strain-Thickened Dilatant Kelvin-Wave Tail Damping: High-wavenumber modes experience enhanced damping $\Gamma_{\mathrm{DDF}}(k) = \alpha k^2(1 + \gamma_{\mathrm{dil}} k^2) > \alpha k^2 = \Gamma_{\mathrm{Newton}}(k)$ via the $+\alpha\gamma_{\mathrm{dil}} k^4 > 0$ shear-thickening term, filtering out short-wavelength components and leaving low-$k$ modes as the late-time power-law tail.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        4. 2D Symplectic Transverse-Traceless (TT) Wave Splat vs. DDF Jamming Contraction & 4D Schur Conditioning: A pure TT wave ($\sigma_{1,2} = \sigma_0 e^{\pm h_+/2}$) preserves $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{TT}} = \sigma_0^4$ and $\mathcal{N}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{TT}}) = (2\pi\sigma_0^2)^{-1}$, whereas DDF longitudinal sheath jamming contracts $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{DDF}} = \sigma_0^4\gamma_\varphi(v)^{-2} < \sigma_0^4$ ($v > 0$) and 4D Schur-complement conditioning $\Sigma_{xx} - \Sigma_{xt}(\nu(\sigma)\Sigma_{tt}^{-1})\Sigma_{tx}$ with dilatant viscosity $\nu(\sigma) = \mu_0(1 + \sigma^2)$ strictly narrows the spatial slice variance.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Master Theorem for Gravitational Waves With DDF (Substrate Strain/Luminosity Decomposition, GPE Vortex Secondary Scattering, Kelvin-Wave Tail Damping, TT vs. Jammed Tensor Splats, & 4D Schur Conditioning): For any sub : DDFSubstrate, re : RiverExterior sub, s : MovingSheath sub, orb : PlanetaryOrbit, and positive parameters $m_2, R, \hbar, m_\phi, g_0, \rho_0, \xi, r, \alpha, \gamma_{\mathrm{dil}}, k, \sigma_0, \mu_0, \Sigma_{tt}^{-1} > 0$:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. DDF Acoustic-Horizon & Dispersed-Phase $(\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)$ Strain/Luminosity Laws:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $h_0^{\mathrm{DDF}} = \frac{r_{H,1}\,r_{H,2}}{R\,a} = \frac{4 G_\phi^2 M m_2 (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)^2}{R\,a}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $(P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{DDF}})^2 = \left(\frac{32}{5}\frac{G_\phi^4 M^2 m_2^2(M+m_2)}{a^5}\right)^2 (\varrho_{\max}^\varphi j_{\min}^\varphi)^5\,\frac{P_{\mathrm{PM}}(e)^2}{\bigl(|w_A^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{GW}})|^2\,|w_B^{\mathbb{C}}(M_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{GW}})|^2\bigr)^7}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. GPE Vortex Core Depletion & Continuous Secondary-Wavelet Scattering (Review-Pop-III-GW-Remnants.md, lines 710–775):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $0 < \operatorname{gpeVortexHealingLength}(\hbar, m_\phi, g_0, \rho_0)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $\operatorname{gpeVortexDensityProfile}(\rho_0, \xi, 0) = 0$ and $\operatorname{gpeVortexDensityProfile}(\rho_0, \xi, \xi) = \rho_0 / 2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $0 < \operatorname{gpeVortexDensityProfile}(\rho_0, \xi, r) < \rho_0$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $\operatorname{gpeVortexScatteringPotential}(\rho_0, \xi, 0) = 0$ and $0 < \operatorname{gpeVortexScatteringPotential}(\rho_0, \xi, r)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. Strain-Thickened Dilatant Kelvin-Wave Tail Damping (Review-Pop-III-GW-Remnants.md, lines 780–855):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $\operatorname{dilatantKelvinTailDampingRate}(\alpha, \gamma_{\mathrm{dil}}, k) - \operatorname{newtonianAcousticDampingRate}(\alpha, k) = \alpha \gamma_{\mathrm{dil}} k^4 > 0$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $\operatorname{newtonianAcousticDampingRate}(\alpha, k) < \operatorname{dilatantKelvinTailDampingRate}(\alpha, \gamma_{\mathrm{dil}}, k)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      4. 2D Symplectic Transverse-Traceless (TT) Wave Splat vs. DDF Jamming Contraction:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{TT}}(h_+) = \sigma_0^4$ and $\mathcal{N}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{TT}}(h_+)) = \frac{1}{2\pi\sigma_0^2}$ for all $h_+ \in \mathbb{R}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • When $0 < s.\mathrm{velocity}$, $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{DDF}}(s) < \det\Sigma_{\mathrm{TT}}(h_+)$, and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      5. 4D Spacetime Tensor Splat Schur-Complement Temporal Conditioning (Review-Pop-III-GW-Remnants.md, lines 535–605):

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3D NormedTensorGaussianSplat3D Gravitational-Wave & Orbital Volume, Bohm Potential, and 3D-to-2D Projection Theorem: Establishes why 3D tensor Gaussian splatting (NormedTensorGaussianSplat3D) is the natural volumetric representation for propagating gravitational waves and inclined orbits, and how 2D NormedTensorGaussianSplat2D arises as its exact orthographic projection:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. Exact 3D-to-2D Orthographic Projections (projectOrthographic2D):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Projecting ttGravitationalWaveSplat3D onto the transverse $(x, y)$ detector plane recovers NormedTensorGaussianSplat2D.ttGravitationalWaveSplat identically,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Projecting ddfGravitationalWaveSplat3D onto the transverse $(x, y)$ plane also recovers ttGravitationalWaveSplat (since DDF longitudinal jamming contracts the 3rd propagation axis $\sigma_3 = \sigma_{z,0}\gamma_\varphi(v)^{-1}$ while preserving the 2D transverse TT polarization ellipse),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Projecting orb.gr36TensorSplat3D onto $(x, y)$ recovers orb.gr24TensorSplat,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. 3D Volumetric Covariance Determinants ($\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}} = \sigma_1^2\sigma_2^2\sigma_3^2$):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Without DDF (pure TT): $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{TT}}(h_+) = \sigma_0^4 \sigma_{z,0}^2$ for all $h_+ \in \mathbb{R}$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • With DDF (longitudinal sheath jamming): $$\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{DDF}}(s, h_+) = \sigma_0^4 \sigma_{z,0}^2 (1 - \beta^2) = \sigma_0^4 \sigma_{z,0}^2 \gamma_\varphi(v)^{-2},$$ and $0 < s.\mathrm{velocity} \implies \det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{DDF}}(s, h_+) < \det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{TT}}(h_+)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • 3D Planetary Orbit: $\det\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{orb}} = \sigma_0^4 \sigma_{z,0}^2 (1 - e^2) = \sigma_0^4 \sigma_{z,0}^2 (p / a)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. 3D Core Bohm Quantum Potential Longitudinal Jamming Increment: $$Q_{\mathrm{core,3D}}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{DDF}}) - Q_{\mathrm{core,3D}}(\Sigma_{\mathrm{3D}}^{\mathrm{TT}}) = \frac{\hbar^2}{4 m \sigma_{z,0}^2}\bigl(\gamma_\varphi(v)^2 - 1\bigr)$$ (the transverse $\sigma_1^{-2} + \sigma_2^{-2} = \sigma_0^{-2}(e^{-h_+} + e^{h_+})$ terms cancel identically).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Complex Grassmannian $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$ Fubini–Study GPE, Dual-Grassmannian iGPE ($\mathbf{Z} \leftrightarrow \mathbf{Z}^\perp$), and Homogeneous Plücker Madelung Hydrodynamics on the Klein Quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{P}^5(\mathbb{C})$ #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Formalizes the complex Grassmannian formulation of the Gross–Pitaevskii equation (GPE), the coupled Dual-Grassmannian interactive/inverse Gross–Pitaevskii (iGPE) system on $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4) \times Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)^\vee$, and the homogeneous Plücker 6-vector Madelung quantum-fluid equations on the Klein quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{P}^5(\mathbb{C})$ without the positive Grassmannian ($Gr^+(2,4)$) restriction (data/chats/Gemini_Grassmannian-Gross-Pitaevskii-Equation-Formulation_20261103-1045.md, lines 1–1458):

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      1. Homogeneous Plücker 6-Vector Calculus, Hodge Duality ($\tilde{p}^I = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon^{IJ}p_J$), Klein Quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4$, & Orthogonal Tangent Projector $\mathcal{H}^{I\bar{J}}$:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Embeds any $2 \times 4$ complex twistor matrix $Z \in \mathbb{C}^{2 \times 4}$ into its 6-component Plücker vector $p(Z) = (\Delta_{01}^{\mathbb{C}}, \Delta_{02}^{\mathbb{C}}, \Delta_{03}^{\mathbb{C}}, \Delta_{12}^{\mathbb{C}}, \Delta_{13}^{\mathbb{C}}, \Delta_{23}^{\mathbb{C}}) \in \mathbb{C}^6$ (twistorToPluckerVec),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Defines the Hodge-dual Plücker 6-vector $\tilde{p} = (p_{34}, -p_{24}, p_{23}, p_{14}, -p_{13}, p_{12})$ (pluckerHodgeDual) and Klein quadric bilinear pairing $\mathcal{C}(p) = \sum_{I=0}^5 p_I \tilde{p}^I = 2(p_{12}p_{34} - p_{13}p_{24} + p_{14}p_{23}) = 0$ (kleinQuadricForm, OnKleinQuadric),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Proves Hodge-dual involution ($\tilde{\tilde{p}} = p$), norm preservation ($\|\tilde{p}\|^2 = \|p\|^2$), and that every $2 \times 4$ twistor matrix lies on the Klein quadric ($\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(\operatorname{twistorToPluckerVec} Z)$),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Defines the intrinsic contravariant Plücker metric operator $\mathcal{H}^{I\bar{J}}(p, \bar{p}) = \|p\|^2 \delta^{IJ} - p^I \bar{p}^J - \overline{\tilde{p}}^I \tilde{p}^J$ (pluckerContravariantMetricApply) using the exact Hermitian quadric normal $n_I(p) = \overline{\tilde{p}_I}$ (pluckerConjHodgeNormal), and proves that on $\mathcal{Q}_4$ it annihilates both radial Euler scaling ($\mathcal{H}\,p = 0$) and Klein quadric normal variations ($\mathcal{H}\,\overline{\tilde{p}} = 0$).
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      2. Canonical Affine Chart $Z = (I_2 \mid W)$ on $Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)$, Fubini–Study Kähler Determinant $\det(I_2 + W W^\dagger) = \|p\|^2 \ge 1$, & Kinetic Norm:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Embeds any $2 \times 2$ complex affine chart $W \in \mathbb{C}^{2 \times 2}$ into $Z = (I_2 \mid W)$ (chartToTwistor),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Proves the Cauchy–Binet Kähler–Plücker identity $\det(I_2 + W W^\dagger) = 1 + \|W\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 + |\det W|^2 = \|p(\operatorname{chartToTwistor} W)\|_{\mathbb{C}^6}^2 \ge 1$ (kahlerDetFactor_eq_pluckerNormSq_and_ge_one), and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Proves that the inverse Fubini–Study metric kinetic norm $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}((I_2 + W W^\dagger) K (I_2 + W^\dagger W) K^\dagger)$ (fubiniStudyKineticNorm) reduces at $W = 0$ to the nonnegative Frobenius norm $\|K\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 \ge 0$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      3. Coupled Dual-Grassmannian iGPE ($Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4) \times Gr_{\mathbb{C}}(2,4)^\vee$), Symplectic Norm Balance, & Chiral Josephson Schubert Tunneling:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Formalizes the coupled primary/dual condensate evolution (CoupledDualGrassmannianState, GrassmannianIGPEFieldState) and proves (grassmannian_igpe_norm_balance_and_josephson_identities) that all real kinetic, Fubini–Study curvature, nonlinear contact, and Hermitian Schubert incidence couplings ($\lambda, \bar{\lambda}$) cancel identically in the total probability rate $\frac{d}{d\tau'}(|\Psi|^2 + |\Phi|^2) = 2 V_{\mathrm{im}}(|\Psi|^2 + |\Phi|^2)$, while individual branch norms exchange probability via the chiral Josephson Schubert current $J_{\mathrm{Josephson}} = 2\operatorname{Im}(\bar{\Psi}\lambda\Phi)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      4. Complex Grassmannian Bogoliubov Dispersion ($R_{\mathrm{Gr}} = 16 \implies \Delta_R = \hbar^2/\mathcal{M}$), Proca Photon Mass, & Critical Deborah Shear-Fracture Threshold ($\mathrm{De}/\mathrm{De}_c \ge 1$):
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Proves (grassmannian_bogoliubov_proca_and_deborah_fracture_identities) that in the repulsive causal sector ($g_{\mathrm{eff}}\rho_0 \ge 0$), $\hbar^2\omega^2 > 0$, whereas in the attractive/non-positive sector ($\lambda = 0, V_{\mathrm{im}} = 0$), tachyonic shear fracture ($\hbar^2\omega^2 \le 0$) holds if and only if the critical Deborah ratio satisfies $\mathrm{De}/\mathrm{De}_c \ge 1$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      5. Homogeneous Plücker Madelung Quantum Hamilton–Jacobi (QHJ), Plücker iGPE Potential Reconstruction, & Self-Dual Weyl Curvature Bridge:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • Formalizes PluckerMadelungState, pluckerQuantumPotential, dualJosephsonPotential, pluckerHamiltonJacobiResidual, pluckerInversePotentialReconstruction, and pluckerBohmWeylCurvatureBridge, and proves (plucker_madelung_qhj_inverse_igpe_and_weyl_bridge_identities) exact Plücker QHJ potential inversion, phase-locked vs. $\pi/2$ chiral phase-slip Josephson exchange, and Weyl curvature reconstruction.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          pluckerHodgeDual (pluckerHodgeDual p) i = p i ∧ pluckerNormSq (pluckerHodgeDual p) = pluckerNormSq p ∧ pluckerNormSq (pluckerConjHodgeNormal p) = pluckerNormSq p ∧ OnKleinQuadric (twistorToPluckerVec Z) ∧ (OnKleinQuadric p → pluckerHermitianInner (pluckerConjHodgeNormal p) p = 0 ∧ pluckerHermitianInner p (pluckerConjHodgeNormal p) = 0 ∧ pluckerContravariantMetricApply p p i = 0 ∧ pluckerContravariantMetricApply p (pluckerConjHodgeNormal p) i = 0)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. Hodge-Dual Involution: $\operatorname{pluckerHodgeDual}(\operatorname{pluckerHodgeDual}(p)) = p$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          2. Norm Preservation: $\|\tilde{p}\|^2 = \|p\|^2$ and $\|\overline{\tilde{p}}\|^2 = \|p\|^2$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          3. Universal Klein Quadric Membership: $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(\operatorname{twistorToPluckerVec}(Z))$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. Hermitian Orthogonality on $\mathcal{Q}_4$: If $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(p)$, then $\langle p, \overline{\tilde{p}}\rangle = 0$ and $\langle \overline{\tilde{p}}, p\rangle = 0$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          5. Exact Radial Euler Scaling Annihilation ($\mathcal{H}\,p = 0$): If $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(p)$, then $\operatorname{pluckerContravariantMetricApply}(p, p) = 0$, and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          6. Exact Klein Quadric Normal Annihilation ($\mathcal{H}\,\overline{\tilde{p}} = 0$): If $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(p)$, then $\operatorname{pluckerContravariantMetricApply}(p, \overline{\tilde{p}}) = 0$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    have Z := chartToTwistor W; Geometry.complexTwoRowMinor Z 0 1 = 1 ∧ Geometry.complexTwoRowMinor Z 2 3 = W 0 0 * W 1 1 - W 0 1 * W 1 0 ∧ kahlerDetFactor W = pluckerNormSq (twistorToPluckerVec Z) ∧ 1 ≤ kahlerDetFactor W ∧ kahlerDetFactor 0 = 1 ∧ fubiniStudyKineticNorm 0 K = fubiniStudyFrobeniusNormSq K ∧ 0 ≤ fubiniStudyKineticNorm 0 K

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Cauchy–Binet Kähler–Plücker Determinant Identity & Fubini–Study Chart Properties: For any affine chart $W \in \mathbb{C}^{2 \times 2}$ and cotangent momentum $K \in \mathbb{C}^{2 \times 2}$, let $Z = \operatorname{chartToTwistor}(W) = (I_2 \mid W)$:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    1. The leading Plücker minor is normalized to unity ($\Delta_{01}^{\mathbb{C}}(Z) = 1$) and the trailing minor equals the $2 \times 2$ determinant ($\Delta_{23}^{\mathbb{C}}(Z) = W_{00} W_{11} - W_{01} W_{10} = \det W$),
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    2. The Fubini–Study Kähler determinant factor $\operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(W) = 1 + \|W\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 + |\det W|^2$ equals the ambient Plücker norm squared $\|p(Z)\|_{\mathbb{C}^6}^2$ of $Z = (I_2 \mid W)$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    3. $1 \le \operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(W)$ (and $0 < \operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(W)$), with equality $\operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(0) = 1$ at the origin $W = 0$, and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    4. At the origin $W = 0$, the inverse Fubini–Study kinetic norm reduces identically to the nonnegative Frobenius norm squared: $\operatorname{fubiniStudyKineticNorm}(0, K) = \operatorname{fubiniStudyFrobeniusNormSq}(K) \ge 0$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Symplectic Norm Balance, Chiral Josephson Tunneling Cancellation, & Unitary Conservation in the Coupled Dual-Grassmannian iGPE: For any s : CoupledDualGrassmannianState:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          1. Primary Branch Continuity with Josephson Tunneling: $\frac{d}{d\tau'}|\Psi|^2 = 2\,V_{\mathrm{im}}\,|\Psi|^2 + J_{\mathrm{Josephson}}(\Psi, \Phi, \lambda)$,

Dual Branch Continuity with Opposite Josephson Tunneling: $\frac{d}{d\tau'}|\Phi|^2 = 2\,V_{\mathrm{im}}\,|\Phi|^2 - J_{\mathrm{Josephson}}(\Psi, \Phi, \lambda)$,

Exact Non-Hermitian Symplectic Norm Balance (igpe_norm_balance_law): All real kinetic, Fubini–Study curvature, nonlinear self-interaction, and Hermitian Schubert cross-coupling ($\pm J_{\mathrm{Josephson}}$) terms cancel identically: $$\frac{d}{d\tau'}\bigl(|\Psi|^2 + |\Phi|^2\bigr) = 2\,V_{\mathrm{im}}\,\bigl(|\Psi|^2 + |\Phi|^2\bigr),$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          4. Unitary Symplectic Conservation in the Hermitian Limit (igpe_unitary_conservation): When $V_{\mathrm{im}} = 0$, $\frac{d}{d\tau'}\bigl(|\Psi|^2 + |\Phi|^2\bigr) = 0$.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Master Theorem for Homogeneous Plücker Madelung QHJ, Plücker iGPE Potential Inversion, Chiral Josephson Phase-Slip Duality, & Self-Dual Weyl Curvature Reconstruction: For any s : PluckerMadelungState with $\hbar \neq 0$ and $\mathcal{M} \neq 0$:
