                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Master Theorem for Revised Turner (2026) Superposition, Gravity (Models 14a/14b), and Gravitational-Wave (Models 14a/14b) Models via Homogeneous Plücker $\mathcal{Q}_4$ Madelung & Dual-Grassmannian iGPE:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                1. Superposition on the Klein Quadric $\mathcal{Q}_4 \subset \mathbb{P}^5(\mathbb{C})$ & Dual-Grassmannian iGPE Equilibrium vs. Chiral Phase-Slip:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • For any complex channel amplitudes $z_1, z_2 \in \mathbb{C}$, the homogeneous Plücker 6-vector $p_{\mathrm{slit}} = \operatorname{twistorToPluckerVec}(\operatorname{complexGr24ChannelMatrix}(z_1, z_2))$ satisfies $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(p_{\mathrm{slit}})$ with $p_{\mathrm{slit}}(0) = z_1$, $p_{\mathrm{slit}}(2) = z_2$, $p_{\mathrm{slit}}(1) = p_{\mathrm{slit}}(3) = p_{\mathrm{slit}}(5) = 1$, and $p_{\mathrm{slit}}(4) = z_1 + z_2 = p_{\mathrm{slit}}(0)\,p_{\mathrm{slit}}(5) + p_{\mathrm{slit}}(2)\,p_{\mathrm{slit}}(3)$, so linear wave superposition is literally enforced by $\mathcal{C}(p_{\mathrm{slit}}) = 0$ on $\mathcal{Q}_4$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the Hermitian phase-locked regime ($s_{\mathrm{pl}}.s_{\mathrm{dual}} = s_{\mathrm{pl}}.s_{\mathrm{real}}, \lambda_{\mathrm{im}} = 0, V_{\mathrm{ext,im}} = 0$), evaluating pluckerMadelungSuperpositionOAMDoubleSlit on $M_{\mathbb{C}}^{\mathrm{DDF}}(s)$ reproduces huygensSteinerOAMDoubleSlit with $\mathcal{V} = \gamma_\varphi(v)^{-1}$ and zero relative predictive error ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$) everywhere.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the chiral $\pi/2$ phase-slip regime ($s_{\mathrm{pl}}.s_{\mathrm{dual}} - s_{\mathrm{pl}}.s_{\mathrm{real}} = \frac{\pi}{2}\hbar$), pluckerMadelungSuperpositionOAMDoubleSlit on a coherent $d_{\mathrm{bary}} = 0$ channel matrix reproduces pilotWaveOAMDoubleSlit with microscopic non-equilibrium offset $\delta_{\mathrm{neq}} = \tau_{\mathrm{flight}}\,\frac{2}{\hbar}\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{pl}}.\rho\,s_{\mathrm{pl}}.\rho_{\mathrm{dual}}}\,\lambda_{\mathrm{re}}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                2. Gravity (Models 14a & 14b): Orbital Kähler–Plücker Identity & Relative Predictive Errors:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • For any orb : PlanetaryOrbit and $\Delta\varpi \in \mathbb{R}$, the Fubini–Study Kähler determinant factor of $W_{\mathrm{orb}} = \mathrm{orb}.\mathrm{gr24AffineChart}(\Delta\varpi)$ satisfies: $$\operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) = \bigl\|p(I_2 \mid W_{\mathrm{orb}})\bigr\|_{\mathbb{C}^6}^2 = 4 - e^2 = 3 + \frac{p}{a} > 3, \qquad \operatorname{kahlerDetFactor}(W_{\mathrm{orb}}) - 3 = 1 - e^2 = \frac{p}{a}.$$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • At solar-system scales ($\delta_{\mathrm{Jos}} = 0$), both Model 14a (turnerPluckerIGPEPrecessionRad) and Model 14b (RiverExterior.turnerDualGr24IGPEDDFPrecessionRad) equal $\Delta\varpi_{\mathrm{GR}} = re.\mathrm{perihelionPrecessionRad}(\mathrm{orb})$ with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$ ($0\%$ error), while for strong-field core shift $\delta_{\mathrm{Jos}} > 0$, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = \delta_{\mathrm{Jos}} / \Delta\varpi_{\mathrm{GR}} > 0$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                3. Gravitational Waves (Models 14a & 14b): Plücker $\mathcal{Q}_4$ Quadrupole Wave & Deborah Shear-Fracture Ringdown:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • The Plücker 6-vector $p_{\mathrm{GW}} = \operatorname{twistorToPluckerVec}(\mathrm{orb}.\mathrm{gr24QuadrupoleWaveMatrix}(\Phi_{\mathrm{orb}}, \Delta\varpi))$ satisfies $\operatorname{OnKleinQuadric}(p_{\mathrm{GW}})$,
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  • In the sub-critical inspiral regime ($\mathrm{De}/\mathrm{De}_c < 1 \implies \delta P_{\mathrm{Jos}} = 0$), both Model 14a (turnerPluckerIGPEGWLuminosity) and Model 14b (RiverExterior.turnerDualGr24IGPEDDFGWLuminosity) equal $P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{GR}} = re.\mathrm{petersMathewsLuminosity}(\mathrm{orb}, m_2)$ with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = 0$ ($0\%$ error), while in the super-critical merger ringdown fracture regime ($\delta P_{\mathrm{Jos}} > 0$), $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} = \delta P_{\mathrm{Jos}} / P_{\mathrm{GW}}^{\mathrm{GR}} > 0$.
